name: North Ridge (Complete)
approach: Primary approach is from the north via the Stuart Lake Trailhead (reached via Icicle Creek Road and FR 7601 out of Leavenworth). From the trailhead, follow the Stuart/Colchuck Lake Trail as it rolls along Mountaineer Creek through forest; at the signed junction roughly 2 miles in, stay left/straight (the Colchuck Lake fork splits right). Continue on the Mountaineer Creek/Stuart Lake trail for about another 0.2 mile, then leave the maintained trail before reaching Stuart Lake itself, cross Mountaineer Creek, and follow its south fork upstream cross-country. After roughly 2 more miles of streamside travel, climb a steep, loose talus/boulder slope to gain the hanging valley beneath Sherpa Peak and the Sherpa Glacier — this valley has good bivy sites and is a common overnight stop. From the valley, angle directly up to the toe of the North Ridge, keeping the Ice Cliff Glacier on your left; the notch/base of the upper ridge sits around 8,200 ft, where a snow-filled gully (often climbed on 4th-class rock at its edge) gains the crest. All-in this is roughly 6-6.5 miles and 3,300+ ft of gain, about 4-5 hours to the base of the climbing. A well-known alternative is the southern approach via the Esmeralda/Teanaway trailhead over Longs Pass and up Ingalls Creek to Goat Pass, gaining the ridge from that side (~9 miles, ~4,800 ft gain, ~8 hours) — longer and higher-gain on the way in, but it sets up a much shorter car-to-car loop for parties planning to descend the Cascadian Couloir, since that descent drops back toward Ingalls Creek. Water is available at Mountaineer Creek and its south fork on the north approach, and at Ingalls Creek/seasonal snow patches near the 8,200 ft notch bivy on the south approach; above the notch there is no reliable water. Route-finding through the boulder/talus slope below Sherpa Glacier and the creek crossing (higher and faster in early season) are the main approach-specific hazards.
